activate.why: House rule: no method longer than 50 lines
House rule: mandatory class member order (logger, constants, fields, constructor, methods)
House rule: logger is 'private static final Logger log'
Spring singletons must not carry non-injected mutable state
Spring beans must be reachable by component scan
No FetchType.EAGER — lazy loading is the JPA default we rely on
Bean Validation must be wired correctly (@Valid on nested/params)
Optional is a return type, never a parameter
Exception handlers keep the original cause (error-handling depth)
Control flow nested at most 3 deep
Files stay under 750 lines of code
No raw generic types
String case/format ops pass an explicit Locale (app is multilingual)
No reliance on the platform default charset
Concurrency: lazy static init is synchronized
Concurrency: no threads started in constructors
Never call System.exit
No floating-point equality checks
Only hash types that define hashCode()
Compare enums with ==
No wildcard imports
Control structures always use braces
One top-level type per file
Prefer switch expressions (Java 21)
Tests: annotated Mockito mocks are initialized
Tests: Mockito matchers used on all arguments
NOSONAR is not allowed — accept/false-positive issues in the UI instead
Same 50-line function limit as the backend
Files stay under 1000 lines of code
Control flow nested at most 3 deep
No 'any' — strict-mode repo
No redundant casts or non-null assertions
No variable shadowing
Unchanged variables are const
Always === / !==
No console.* logging left in app code
No commented-out code
No unused function parameters
Merge collapsible if statements
Functions return consistently
No redundant await
Don't declare-then-immediately-return
Tests: no trivially-true assertions
Tests: one async completion style per callback
